It was like a month that they were trapped, at least, if not longer. So, you know they've probably scattered, but at least get word that they're alive. But he says we don't intend to spend long there. Outfit a new ship as quickly as possible, and then sail who knows where. Unless he says, everything goes south on your mission in Drankor, in which case we'll flee south and raise an army and see what we can do."

So you get settled. You say your goodbyes. Milo and Tilly sail off on the ship on the folding boat. Quiet settles over the group as you begin to contemplate your next move which must presumably be heading for Drankor, but exactly how and what you intend is part of the sort of role-playing objective for the evening.

markers.note: Arrival is aboard the departing boat, not at the intended western islands; no later destination arrival is recorded.

markers.reading: The party flies aboard Vindristjarna from the southern ocean across the coast and inland above the Istaros/jungle, reaching a position fifteen miles south of Drankor by the next morning.

evidence.quote: Faldrak goes and sets a course.

So the ship begins to move as the rain clouds finally break and a brief afternoon thunderstorm breaks out. Everybody retreats inside, the giant pile of treasure still, partially sitting on the deck as the rain falls.

Yeah, it's mostly gold. It's not going to really be affected by rain. So the ship begins to move. You can see. I mean, you can see the coastline right? You're high enough up. It's only 60 miles away. The coast is visible, and you begin to depart the storm and travel across, the still strangely wavy sea, despite the, you know, mostly blue clouds, although passing thunderstorms right now. Heading for the mouth of the Istaros, the river that goes all the way to Isingue and north, on which Drankor sits.

You're sitting around talking at dinner, as the ship now crosses, after sunset, from the ocean to the land near the mouth of this giant river, as you begin to travel, following the river, for now. Inland towards Drankor, probably 12 h away. So you'd if you just kept going, you'd reach there a couple hours after dawn. Maybe 8 in the morning. That you still have some time to decide what to do. You'll be 20 miles away at dawn. Sun rises. Yeah.

Yeah, that would. That would take 16 would take an extra 24 min. That's not that long. So you rest for the night, as the ship continues to travel, in a straight path over the jungles, towards the city of Drankor.

And over the course of 12 h, ending around 7 in the morning, as you wake up and look across the jungle, now about 15 miles from the city of Drankor, a second copy of Delwath leaps up from where pile of ice and snow once was. And you look across the jungle. And you can see the the line of the river now, winding below you and stretching off to the west.
So you are now as dawn breaks about 15 miles away almost directly due south above the river, probably visible if anybody's watching.

route.reading: Cross the coastline after sunset and follow the river inland.
Continue over jungle and the Istaros toward Drankor.

markers.reading: Delwath’s earlier scry shows the Seeker, Riswynn and Kenzo doubles standing on the docks, with neither Wellby nor Delwath visible.

evidence.quote: Wait. What happened to my scry of Seeker?
DM: When are you scrying? Yeah, that it Seeker failed.
Delwath: That was last night. That was before we even did anything.
DM: Okay, Seeker and Riswynn and Kenzo are standing on the docks. Looking sort of glassy eyed a little bit, staring out at the river. You do not see Wellby or Delwath.

They're just standing there, I mean, I'll watch for 10 min. Is there anything interesting? Is there any other things moving around that I can see like there's no like zombies crawling up out of the river, or anything. Are there?
DM: Not not at the docks. No. Yeah, they don't. They don't. I mean, they don't seem to be doing much like they're just kind of standing there like they're not even really talking.
Delwath: The right— half deactivated.
DM: They're like, yeah, they're like, half deactivated. Standby mode.

markers.note: The table places this resolved scry on the previous evening/night during the voyage.

markers.reading: From fifteen miles south the party sees the ruined city, a surviving tower, the docks, the temple dome and the open plaza through the jungle.

evidence.quote: From the from the shores of the river, you can—I mean, this is all like a pretty dense jungle, but you can see bits of the ruined city poking out. Now, as you're close enough, you can see what you guess must be the tallest of what the report you saw described as the teeth of Drankor standing 200 feet tall or more—it's hard to judge—but above the trees, with the crystal dome, and on its top tinted in blue and gold, still standing intact. You can see the line of the docks just in the distance, not the full like the river twists, and you can't see the. You can't see the full extent of the docks, but you can see a part of a clearing where the trees don't approach to the river. And there's this long, wide promenade, this marble road that runs along the edge of the river. Still gleaming seeming as new.

DM: Turning your gaze inland, you can see it's mostly trees, but you see you know the occasional tower or dome poking out from the trees that is still intact. And one much bigger than any temple you've seen before you know. It's sort of like the the dome of the Duomo, but even bigger than that, standing and stretching still intact. The trees clear around it. This must be the dome of the Temple of the 8 Divines, that where Rai was.

DM: And you can see just in a few places through the trees this road that leads from the docks inland to this great plaza. Huge open space that where no trees grow which you can. Still, you can see from your perspective here maybe half a mile inland. It's a fairly compact city.

DM: Okay this grand open plaza with you can't really see the details at this distance. Right? You just see this open space. And you see in places you don't. You don't see any, you know, whatever was described as this grand tomb, at least at least not from here. But there is a a. There's the plaza, and then there's a bit of a rise of the land, and then there's more of the city behind this sort of rise of the land, perhaps, and you do. You do see places where there are like, there's mists hanging around the trees, sitting on the water are tinged reddish in places. Some of this is probably just the dawn of the jungle. But clearly there's also lingering patches of this sort of plague echoes that you saw and avoided and heard about from the dragonets on the circular island, but seemed to also spread throughout this ruined city.
DM: So you are now as dawn breaks about 15 miles away almost directly due south above the river, probably visible if anybody's watching.

markers.reading: Kenzo senses Wellby’s double hiding among the ruined warehouses/shops near the other three on the docks; Delwath’s double remains atop the tower.

evidence.quote: I will. I will focus then as well, just to try to get more resolution if I can.

markers.reading: The party approaches to about a mile from Drankor, pauses as the tower charges, then reverses to hover a little farther out.

evidence.quote: Delwath short rests as the Vindristjarna creeps closer, traveling up the river.

DM: The sky seems to grow a little dim as you approach. When you get about 5 miles out, you begin to feel this presence, this darkness pressing against you, only the light of the Bahrâzel keeping you from descending into fear and terror.

DM: The 2 halflings who are not—the Copperharps—are like huddled in a corner, like sort of just holding each other, and, you know telling each other stories as they shiver in fear, while the rest of your crew is at least outwardly unaffected by this sense as you feel like you're pressing forward. I need some darker music here. As you feel like you're pressing forward into against some will that sets itself against your own.

DM: You press forward for the next 20 min, 2 miles closer, 30 min. It's now maybe 8 30 in the morning. 40, 50 min pass. You're about a mile away from the city when the sky begins to darken again, and you hear a peal of thunder.
DM: And there's a bright spot glowing where the tower sits.
Faldrak looks over at Seeker like, "Do we keep going, boss?"
Seeker: I'll say, "Hold up! We're gonna pause here."
DM: The ship stops.
You're about to get hit by lightning. Yeah, that's what I was. Faldrak's asking what you want to do.
Seeker: Back, back it up a little bit.
DM: Puts the ship in reverse, and like waits hovering a little more than a mile from the city.

markers.note: The lightning is threatened, not resolved as a strike. The party never reaches the tower or docks.

markers.reading: Vindristjarna turns west, circles the city for about twenty minutes, and reaches its western edge, away from the southeast tower.

evidence.quote: Okay. So the ship turns west.
Riswynn: And circles the city.
Tower is at the southeast corner of the city.
Delwath: So let's go to the northwest corner.

DM: Okay? So you fly around. You travel for, you know, 20 min or something like that. Flying through the jungle you can see below you. Now you're close enough. You can see this grand plaza, I mean, there's still some roads that cut through. The trees haven't overgrown the roads. It seems like there was once, I mean there's a grid. And there was all of these big like manors and villas, with courtyards that are all just wracked with trees growing through them.

As you find yourself now on the western edge of the city, the red mists in Apollyon's tomb to the northeast; the Grand Plaza and the temple of the divine—the 8 divines to the sort of southeast, and then the expanse of the jungle, broken by these kind of occasional towers and and domes that stick up from the canopies of the trees and small glimpses of the forest. You're about a mile and a half from the tower and the docks. It's up to you where you want to land and what your approach is going to be. Anybody.

duration.basis: DM describes the circling flight as twenty minutes or something like that.

markers.note: The party sees the plaza, temple and tomb valley from above; the route does not establish landings or entry at any of them.

Delwath: Yeah, yeah, I'll do it. Yeah, yeah, that makes sense.
